title: The Sun at millimeter wavelengths. IV. Magnetohydrodynamic waves in small-scale bright features
question: Identify and study magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves and their energy flux in bright small-scale magnetic features in the solar chromosphere using ALMA Band 3 and Band 6 observations alongside Bifrost simulations.

data.arrays: Interferometric array and (single-dish) Total Power antennas
data.angular_resolution: Band 3: ~2.2 arcsec x 1.7 arcsec (1600 km x 1235 km); Band 6: ~0.84 arcsec x 0.67 arcsec (610 km x 488 km)

what.value: 3D RMHD Bifrost simulation of a magnetic enhanced network region surrounded by quiet Sun

evidence.quote: The simulation used here was created with the 3D radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code Bifrost (cite: 2011A&A...531A.154G) and represents a magnetic enhanced network region surrounded by quiet Sun (cite: 2016A&A...585A...4C).

what.value: Reconstructed ALMA Band 3 and Band 6 time series (SALSA data sets D02 and D08) and magnetic topology characterization

evidence.quote: These data products are presented in (cite: 2021RSPTA.37900174J) as data sets D2 and D8, where they showed that the magnetic topology at chromospheric heights represents vertical or near-vertical fields in a large portion of the FoVs with more inclined field towards the edges.
The specific time series used in this study can be downloaded from the Solar ALMA Science Archive (SALSA) as data sets D02 (Band 3) and D08 (Band 6) (cite: 2022A&A...659A..31H).

recipe.goal: Synthesize and degrade simulation continuum brightness temperature maps to match ALMA observations
recipe.method: Solve radiative transfer with ART on Bifrost simulation snapshots to get Band 3 and Band 6 brightness temperatures, subsample frames to 2 s cadence with scan gaps matching ALMA, convolve with the median ALMA synthetic elliptical beam, and rebin pixels to ALMA pixel sizes.
key_parameters: Degraded pixel sizes: 0.34 arcsec (Band 3) and 0.14 arcsec (Band 6)
assumptions: LTE radiative transfer using non-equilibrium electron densities from Bifrost; perfect spatial Fourier space sampling approximated by Gaussian beam convolution

recipe.goal: Automatically identify, segment, track, and classify oscillating small-scale bright features
recipe.method: Apply a Difference of Gaussians (DoG) filter to each frame, find local maxima, segment features via Flood fill on normalized inverted images, filter out elongated/large masks, track overlapping masks frame-to-frame, and cluster extracted peak-temperature light curves using DBSCAN to select oscillating features.
key_parameters: DoG filter Gaussian widths: 0.5 and 2.0 times the median major axis of the ALMA beam; local maxima minimum separation: 1.5 times the median major beam

Flood fill tolerance: ~2.4 standard deviations (FWHM halfway between seed peak temperature and FoV median temperature); max border distance filter: 4 times median beam major axis; frame-to-frame overlap: >= 2 pixels
assumptions: Merged features terminate the lifespan of the individual merging features at the previous frame

recipe.goal: Extract physical properties, sizes, and horizontal velocities of tracked features
recipe.method: For each feature and frame, extract peak brightness temperature, compute equivalent circular diameter from mask area, track intensity-weighted centre of gravity to compute instantaneous horizontal velocities, and take the FFT of horizontal velocity oscillations to extract velocity amplitudes.
key_parameters: FFT velocity amplitude threshold: > 2 standard deviations above the average
assumptions: 1 arcsec ~ 727 km; features are approximately circular (blob-like) so diameter of a circle of equal area represents feature size

recipe.goal: Determine oscillation periods and temperature-size phase differences via wavelet analysis
recipe.method: Detrend temperature, size, and horizontal velocity time series with a linear fit, apodize with a Tukey window, and compute Continuous Wavelet Transforms (CWT) and cross-wavelet transforms between temperature and size.
key_parameters: Linear detrending; Tukey window length = 0.1; CWT significance threshold >= 95% confidence level outside the cone of influence

recipe.goal: Estimate wave energy flux of sausage modes
recipe.method: Compute filling factor f, radial velocity perturbation v_r from radius amplitude and size period, phase speed v_ph from temperature and area fractional perturbations, and combine with external mass density rho_e from the Bifrost simulation using Eq. 1.
key_parameters: Observing frequencies: nu = 100 GHz (Band 3) and 240 GHz (Band 6); External mass density rho_e = 2.5e-8 kg m^-3 (Band 3) and 4.0e-7 kg m^-3 (Band 6)
Degraded simulation median formation heights: 1563 km (Band 3) and 1260 km (Band 6)
assumptions: External mass densities rho_e for ALMA observations are taken from the Bifrost simulation (within circles of 3x feature radius outside the feature); ALMA brightness temperature in Rayleigh-Jeans limit is a proxy for emission intensity

score_reason: The science-ready ALMA data cubes (D02 and D08) and auxiliary reader (SALAT) are publicly downloadable from SALSA, and the image segmentation, tracking, wavelet, and wave energy flux equations are described in detail with explicit thresholds. However, the custom tracking/DBSCAN/wavelet scripts are not released and DBSCAN hyperparameters are not stated.
rediscovery_reason: The exact calibrated and reconstructed ALMA solar cubes (D02 and D08) are publicly available on SALSA, the DoG + flood-fill + tracking + CWT + energy flux pipeline is well-specified, and the main results are concrete numeric values (feature counts, oscillation periods, phase speeds, radial velocities, and wave energy fluxes).
